newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes lower on late commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes lower on late commercial selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed lower after running into late commercial selling although losses were limited by crusher buying, floor sources said.
"Crushers were big buyers in both March and November. If they hadn't been here we would have been quite a bit lower," one WCE oilseed trader said.
Lower CBOT soybean oil and concern the continued strength of the Canadian dollar versus the yen would adversely impact export demand, were the main bearish influences.
The key old crop contract, March, ended $1.60 lower at $407.70 while new crop November closed off $1.30 at $374.80.
Flaxseed also finished lower, weakened by late hedge selling in quiet trading. March ended off $1.80 at $353.20.

Western barley futures closed mixed with volume boosted by active February/March and February/May spread trading. Dealers said Benson Quinn was the major buyer of the February/March spread with UGG and Cargill noted sellers.
Feed wheat also ended mixed, underpinned by scale down commercial buying with Cargill featured. March closed up $0.80 at $169.00. May feed peas ended up US$1.50 at US$195.50. Oats were tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
